newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC orders PJM to revise power pool plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC orders PJM to revise power pool plan.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Wednesday ordered utilities in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) power pool to revise their two competing proposals for restructuring their pool.

The two plans called for an independent system operator (ISO) to handle all transmission in the pool, but the Commission said that both failed to meet its guidelines to ensure that the ISO was truly independent of the utilities.
Commissioners criticized the two plans, saying the ISO's board would have been dominated by PJM members at the expense of others, such as marketers, an FERC spokeswoman said.

The Commission also ordered the utilities to file a new pool-wide tariff, by December 31, reflecting requirements in the FERC's Order 888, which called for utilities to open their transmission lines to all competing power producers.
The existing PJM proposals failed to meet the requirements that the utilities should offer the same service to themselves and all other power producers and marketers, FERC said.

While it did not require utilities to set up independent operators, in its effort to promote power market competition, FERC encouraged the formation of ISOs to ensure that utilities did not discriminate against other power producers.
The commission said Wednesday that an independent operator should be able to develop its own operating procedures and ensure reliability of power grid operations.
It should also control all transmission facilities in its region; identify transmission constraints; coordinate with neighboring grid areas; and make all transmission information accessible.
The commission encouraged the 10 utilities in PJM to agree on a single plan for restructuring the pool.

Competing PJM plans were submitted by PECO Energy Co and the nine other utilities in the pool -- Atlantic Energy Inc, Baltimore Gas and Electric, Delmarva Power and Light Co, PP&L Resources Inc, Potomac Electric Power Co, Public Service Enterprise Group Inc, and three GPU Inc utilities.
